IS-4_1.title: Understanding the Organization and Its Context
IS-4_1.description: The company names what inside it and around it bears on its information security: what it does and where, the laws and contracts it answers to, and the threats it faces. Scope, risks and objectives are planned against this picture.

IS-4_2.title: Understanding the Needs and Expectations of Interested Parties
IS-4_2.description: The company lists who has a stake in its information security, such as customers, authorities, staff, suppliers and owners, what each of them expects of it, and which of those expectations its ISMS takes on.

IS-4_3.title: Determining the Scope of the Information Security Management System
IS-4_3.description: The company sets the boundaries of its ISMS: which sites, systems, teams and services it covers, which it leaves out, and why. The scope is written down so that staff and auditors work from the same one.

IS-4_4.title: Information Security Management System
IS-4_4.description: Information security is run as a managed system that is set up, operated, kept current and improved over time. The clauses that follow are its parts.

IS-5_1.title: Leadership and Commitment
IS-5_1.description: Top management leads the ISMS: it backs the policy and the objectives, provides people and budget, makes security part of how the business runs and holds the people involved to it.

IS-5_2.title: Policy
IS-5_2.description: Top management sets the information security policy: what security means for this company, the frame for its objectives and the commitment to keep improving. Staff know the policy. Recommendation: one or two pages, reviewed together with the management review.

IS-5_3.title: Organizational Roles, Responsibilities and Authorities
IS-5_3.description: Top management decides who is responsible for what in information security, including who runs the ISMS and who reports on it, and tells the people concerned.

IS-6_1.title: Actions to Address Risks and Opportunities
IS-6_1.description: The company plans how it deals with risks and opportunities for its information security: the method for assessing risks (how they are found, analysed and rated, and when a risk is acceptable), the treatment chosen for each risk, and the Statement of Applicability (SoA), which lists the controls the company applies and those it leaves out. Recommendation: give a reason for every control left out.

IS-6_2.title: Information Security Objectives and Planning to Achieve Them
IS-6_2.description: The company sets measurable information security objectives that follow from the policy, and plans how, by whom and by when each one is reached and checked.

IS-6_3.title: Planning of Changes
IS-6_3.description: When the ISMS itself has to change, the change is planned before it is made.

IS-7_1.title: Resources
IS-7_1.description: The company provides the people, time, money and tools the ISMS needs to work and to improve.

IS-7_2.title: Competence
IS-7_2.description: The company decides what people with security tasks need to know and be able to do, closes gaps through training, hiring or outside help, and keeps proof of their competence.

IS-7_3.title: Awareness
IS-7_3.description: Everyone working for the company knows the security policy, their own part in it, and what follows when the rules are not kept.

IS-7_4.title: Communication
IS-7_4.description: The company agrees who communicates which security matters, to whom and how, inside the company and to the outside.

IS-7_5.title: Documented Information
IS-7_5.description: The company keeps the documents and records its ISMS needs and manages them: who writes and approves them, where the current version is, who may see them and how long they are kept.

IS-8_1.title: Operational Planning and Control
IS-8_1.description: The plans from clause 6 are carried out in daily operation, including work done by suppliers, with records that show the processes ran as intended.

IS-8_2.title: Information Security Risk Assessment
IS-8_2.description: The company assesses its information security risks with the method set under 6.1, repeats the assessment regularly and after significant changes, and keeps the results.

IS-8_3.title: Information Security Risk Treatment
IS-8_3.description: The company carries out its risk treatment plan and keeps the results.

IS-9_1.title: Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis and Evaluation
IS-9_1.description: The company decides what it measures about information security and how, collects the figures, and evaluates whether the ISMS and its controls work.

IS-9_2.title: Internal Audit
IS-9_2.description: The company audits its ISMS internally on a regular basis, with auditors who do not audit their own work, and keeps the audit programme and the results.

IS-9_3.title: Management Review
IS-9_3.description: Top management reviews the ISMS regularly, based on audit results, measurements, incidents and changes, and decides what to improve.

IS-10_1.title: Continual Improvement
IS-10_1.description: The company keeps making its ISMS a better fit and more effective, using what audits, reviews and incidents show.

IS-10_2.title: Nonconformity and Corrective Action
IS-10_2.description: When something does not meet a requirement, the company fixes it, deals with the consequences, removes the cause so that it does not recur, checks that the fix worked and keeps a record.
